rationale: Olden/health is a tiny (2366 text bytes, 14 functions) pointer- and list-heavy simulation with a hot recursive driver (sim) and small helper functions, so the table favors cheap, low-risk transformations (SUB, SPLIT, IGV) with high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights and near-zero RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights, letting them apply broadly without bloating the minute binary; FLA gets the highest SecurityGain weight because flattening the sim/get_results control flow yields the strongest resistance, but moderate RuntimeCost and elevated CorrectnessRisk weights keep it off the hottest recursive traversal loops where the dispatch loop and pointer churn hurt most; BCF is deliberately constrained by very high SizeCost (0.9) and RuntimeCost (0.8) weights since bogus basic blocks would multiply a 2.3KB text section and slow the patient-list inner loops, restricting it to large cold functions like sim's cold paths; IBR and ICALL carry elevated CorrectnessRisk weights (0.6/0.5) because health is built around linked-list pointer traversal and indirect calls through function pointers where indirect dispatch rewriting can misfire, and moderate RuntimeCost weights reflect that indirect jumps on the hot simulation loop are costly; overall the profile pushes the compiler toward dense cheap diversification everywhere plus targeted flattening, keeping overhead acceptable and correctness intact.
